minutes.headline: Select Board heard a clean FY22 audit and a Flat Hill drainage study, and recommended two town meeting articles.
minutes.summary: The auditors reported an unmodified opinion with no deficiencies and strong reserves. The board then spent a long stretch on Flat Hill Road drainage, where the engineer said maintenance of private basins is the first step and a real fix needs land for detention. The board recommended warrant articles 3 and 14, appointed a 300th anniversary committee member, ratified beach staff, and went into executive session on the fire union.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to recommend two annual town meeting articles: prior year invoices paid from free cash, and the FY2024 sewer enterprise budget.
The sewer enterprise budget was revised to cut capital spending to cover Fitchburg rate increases and retiree costs, and the board recommended it.
The auditors presented the FY22 audit, with federal awards audited with no findings and the town's pension and retiree health liabilities both described as lower.
The board spent a long stretch on Flat Hill Road drainage with no resolution; the engineer will look at a modified detention system in the town right of way and size the land needed.
The board appointed a 300th anniversary committee member and ratified the town manager's seasonal beach staff appointments.

why_it_matters: The two recommended articles, one drawing on free cash and one setting the sewer budget, go to residents at annual town meeting, where they will be asked to vote on them.
Any fix for Flat Hill Road flooding that needs land or a detention system would be a capital cost to the town, and the minutes give no cost or funding source for it yet.
watch_next: Engineer's sizing of a modified detention system and the land it would need on Flat Hill Road.
Annual town meeting votes on articles 3 and 14, and on the opioid stabilization article, which Town Counsel is reviewing.
